partner_context.their_ambition: The Rotterdam-The Hague transport authority (MRDH) oversees the Waterbus — the largest public-transport ferry system in the Netherlands — running fast commuter boats along the Nieuwe Maas between Rotterdam, Dordrecht and the Drechtsteden. New electric Waterbus vessels are already entering the fleet. The authority's ambition is a fast, zero-emission river network that keeps commuters off congested roads.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the foiling-electric upgrade to a river network MRDH already runs and is already electrifying. The Rotterdam–Dordrecht commuter spine and the Drechtsteden links — flown clear of the water: faster, near-silent, low-wake and zero-emission, on the same OV-chipkaart, from the Waterbus stops that already exist.

hero.eyebrow: Authority proposal · Rotterdam, Netherlands · MRDH (Rotterdam-The Hague transport authority)
hero.title: Navier × Rotterdam Waterbus — the Nieuwe Maas, on foils
hero.subtitle: A zero-emission foiling layer on the Waterbus commuter spine — Rotterdam to Dordrecht and the Drechtsteden: faster, quieter and all-electric on the river network MRDH already runs and is already electrifying.
hero.what_we_do_together: MRDH brings the Waterbus network, the stops and the public-transport mandate; Navier brings the foiling-electric fleet, captain training and the certification path. Together we run the same river — faster and zero-emission — extending the electrification the Waterbus has already begun.

why_now: New electric Waterbus vessels are already entering service, and the authority is under pressure to make the longer river runs faster and greener to keep them competitive with the road. The stops are in place and the mandate is clear; a foiling-electric fleet is how the Rotterdam–Dordrecht spine gets meaningfully faster while going fully clean, with low wake on a busy commercial river.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the MRDH network at Erasmusbrug/Willemsplein, steps from the metro and tram. A commuter steps off the metro and straight onto a foil down the Nieuwe Maas to Dordrecht — faster than the road, on the same OV-chipkaart — while the conventional Waterbus keeps the short high-frequency hops underneath.

differentiation.why_navier: The platform is purpose-built for this network: 10x more efficient than a planing hull, low-wake (vital on shared and protected waters), near-silent, zero-emission, and viable year-round. It delivers the authority's published decarbonisation commitment on the links where speed and wake have kept older vessels in service.

proof_points.claim: The Waterbus is the Netherlands' largest public-transport ferry.
proof_points.evidence: The MRDH Waterbus runs scheduled commuter boats along the Nieuwe Maas between Rotterdam, Dordrecht and the Drechtsteden.
New electric Waterbus vessels are entering service on the network.
The Netherlands targets deep emissions cuts by 2030 and climate neutrality by 2050, with public-transport authorities decarbonising their fleets.

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

objections.concern: Will it slow down a busy commercial river?
objections.response: No — the platform is low-wake and precise; it keeps to the Waterbus corridors and shares the Nieuwe Maas courteously with commercial traffic.

objections.concern: Some Waterbus lines are under budget pressure — how does this help?
objections.response: Speed changes the economics: a foiling run is faster than the road on the longer links, which is what makes river public transport competitive enough to defend.

objections.concern: Does this replace the Waterbus people rely on?
objections.response: No — the conventional Waterbus keeps the short high-frequency hops; foiling adds a faster, cleaner layer on the longer commuter spine.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling-electric fleet, captain training, and the maintenance and certification path.
the_ask.partner_brings: The ferry route map, the piers/stops, the single-ticket integration, and the published decarbonisation mandate.
the_ask.next_step: Identify the first Waterbus link — most likely the Rotterdam–Dordrecht commuter spine — for a foiling-electric public pilot on the OV-chipkaart.

close.body: The Waterbus is already the country's biggest public ferry, and it's already going electric. Navier is how its longer river runs get fast enough to beat the road — a quiet, zero-emission ride from Rotterdam to Dordrecht and the Drechtsteden, on the same public ticket, and gentle on a working river.
